QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_42

question.text: Over-claiming of impact is a common SIA challenge. Which techniques are recommended in Section 5.12 to mitigate it?

answer.text: Assigning roles to intervening variables, capturing quality-of-life indicators by stakeholders, and using dead-weight adjustments
Compounding all beneficiary responses regardless of overlap
Ignoring intervening variables to keep the report simple
Only counting direct, un-triangulated beneficiary testimony

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.12 Challenges states: 'Over claiming of impact needs to be addressed. Assigning roles to intervening variables, capturing quality of life indicators by stakeholders and using dead weights can avoid over claiming.' The Trap: B is the classic over-claim mistake (double counting). C ignores a standard remedy. D actively amplifies over-claim. Cross-Exam Context: Deadweight is a term used in development economics; XXIII tests it as practical SIA procedure. Assessor's Pro-Tip: In your AIR, report 'gross impact' and 'net impact after deadweight/displacement' separately — reviewers prefer to see the adjustment, and the SE benefits by demonstrating methodological rigour to investors/donors.
